_note: Charters for the realization pilot (realization_pilot.py). from_run: Identity's real charter from a saved run (runs/<id>/goal.json). charter: written by hand for the pilot, marked synthetic. The pilot plans and judges only; nothing is built.

briefs.label: Brew Lab cafe site with pre-order (real charter)
Phone number change (synthetic, must stay tiny)

charter.statement: Change the phone number shown on the Brew Lab website from +91 80 4123 0000 to +91 98200 12345.
charter.audience: Visitors to the Brew Lab website.
standards: Nothing else on the page changes.
rules: Change only the phone number.
done_when: The page shows the phone number +91 98200 12345 wherever it showed a phone number before.
The number +91 80 4123 0000 no longer appears anywhere on the page.

charter.statement: A phone-friendly web app where people in Indiranagar, Bengaluru order food from local restaurants for delivery, aiming for 10,000 users in its first year.
charter.audience: People ordering food in Indiranagar; local restaurant owners; delivery riders.
standards: Works on a phone first.
Payments by UPI and card through a licensed payment gateway.
Prices shown in rupees including taxes and fees.
rules: Only restaurants with a valid FSSAI licence are listed.
No customer data is sold or shared for marketing.
done_when: Customers can browse restaurants by cuisine and see each restaurant's menu with prices.
Customers can add items to a cart and pay by UPI or card.
Customers see the status of their order from placed to delivered.
Restaurants have a page where they accept or decline incoming orders and mark them ready.
Each order is assigned to a rider, and the rider sees pickup and drop-off details.
Each restaurant page shows its FSSAI licence number, and the app has a privacy policy.
The fee model (commission, delivery fee) is written down with its expected margin per order.
There is a written plan for reaching the first 1,000 orders, with the channels to try.

briefs.label: Personal loan app under RBI digital lending rules (synthetic)

charter.statement: A phone-friendly web app where salaried people in India apply for a personal loan of Rs 50,000 to Rs 5,00,000 from Kanak Finance, an RBI-registered NBFC.
charter.audience: Salaried people in India aged 21 to 58.
standards: Works on a phone first.
Follows the RBI digital lending rules that apply to an NBFC.
rules: No loan is disbursed by the app itself; it collects the application and shows the offer.
Customer data is used only for this application, with consent.
done_when: An eligibility checker asks for age, monthly income and city, and says whether the person can apply.
The application form collects name, PAN, employer, monthly income and loan amount, and validates PAN format.
A KYC step collects identity proof before an offer is shown.
Before accepting, the customer sees a Key Fact Statement with the annual percentage rate, all fees and the repayment schedule.
The customer gives explicit consent for each use of their data, and can see what they consented to.
The app shows the grievance redressal officer's name and contact, and the lender's RBI registration.
The customer can see the status of their application.

briefs.label: Marketing plan for a product launch (synthetic)

charter.statement: A marketing plan to launch FitBowl, a Bengaluru meal-prep subscription for office workers, and reach 500 paying subscribers in the first 90 days.
charter.audience: The FitBowl founders, who will carry out the plan; their target customers are office workers aged 24 to 40 in Bengaluru.
standards: Every channel has a budget in rupees and a target number.
Claims about health or food follow FSSAI advertising rules.
rules: The total marketing budget is Rs 3,00,000 for 90 days.
No paid fake reviews or bought followers.
done_when: The plan names the target customer segments, with the size of each in Bengaluru and where the figure comes from.
It names at least three competitors with their price per meal and how FitBowl is different.
It states FitBowl's positioning in one sentence and the three key messages.
It lists the channels to use, each with its budget, expected cost per subscriber and target subscribers, adding up to 500 and Rs 3,00,000.
It has a week-by-week launch calendar for the 90 days.
It defines how each channel's results are measured and when a channel is stopped.
Every health claim in the messages is marked as allowed or not allowed under FSSAI advertising rules.

charter.statement: A business plan and a 12-slide investor pitch deck for KiranaLink, an app that lets neighbourhood grocery shops in Pune take orders on WhatsApp, to raise a Rs 2 crore seed round.
charter.audience: Seed investors in India; the founders presenting it.
standards: Every number has a source or is marked as an assumption.
The deck works without the presenter talking.
rules: No invented customer names, logos or quotes.
Revenue projections are labelled as projections.
done_when: The plan sizes the market (total, serviceable and obtainable) with sources or stated assumptions.
It describes the customer problem with evidence and the solution.
It compares at least three competitors or alternatives.
It states the business model: who pays, how much and how often.
It has a 3-year financial projection with revenue, costs, burn and the month the company breaks even.
It says how the Rs 2 crore will be spent and what milestones it reaches.
The pitch deck has 12 slides that follow the plan, and every number on a slide matches the plan.

charter.statement: A 4-week online course teaching shop owners in small Indian towns to sell on Instagram, in plain English with Hindi terms where useful.
charter.audience: Owners of small shops with no marketing training who use a smartphone daily.
standards: Each lesson takes 15 minutes or less.
Plain language: no marketing jargon without a one-line meaning.
rules: No promises of guaranteed sales.
Examples use made-up shops, clearly marked as examples.
done_when: The course states 4 to 6 learning outcomes a learner can do at the end.
It has 4 modules, one per week, each with 3 to 5 lessons and the outcome each lesson serves.
Every lesson has a short script, one worked example and one practice task.
Each module ends with a 5-question quiz with answers and a one-line reason for each answer.
There is a final assignment with a marking rubric.
There is a one-page guide for the learner on how to take the course.

charter.statement: An Android and iOS app for a Chennai gym chain where members book classes, see their attendance and renew membership.
charter.audience: Members of the gym chain's 6 branches; front-desk staff.
standards: Meets Google Play and Apple App Store review guidelines.
Works on phones from Android 10 and iOS 15.
rules: Payments for membership go through the stores' rules or a licensed gateway as the rules allow.
Members' health data is stored only with their consent.
done_when: Members can sign in with their phone number and a one-time password.
Members can see the class timetable of any branch and book or cancel a class.
Members see their attendance for the last 3 months.
Members can renew their membership and get a receipt.
Staff can see bookings per class and mark attendance.
The app has a privacy policy and a data-deletion request option, as the stores require.
There is a release checklist for both stores: listing text, screenshots, age rating and review notes.

charter.statement: A customer support chatbot for an online electronics store that answers order, return and warranty questions and hands over to a person when it can't help.
charter.audience: Customers of the store across India; the store's 5-person support team.
standards: Answers in English and Hindi.
Never states an order detail it has not looked up.
rules: It cannot issue refunds itself.
It follows the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules for return and grievance information.
done_when: It answers the 20 most common questions, listed with the answer it gives to each.
It looks up an order's status from an order number and says where the order is.
It explains the return policy and starts a return request with the order number and reason.
It hands the chat to a person when asked, when it fails twice, or when the customer is upset, with the chat history.
It shows the grievance officer's name and contact when asked about complaints.
There is a test set of 50 questions with the expected answer, and it passes at least 45.

charter.statement: A Chrome extension that shows the price history of a product while the user is on Amazon.in or Flipkart, so shoppers can tell if a sale is real.
standards: Meets the Chrome Web Store policies.
Asks for the fewest permissions possible.
rules: No browsing data leaves the device except the product id being looked up.
No affiliate links are added without telling the user.
done_when: On a product page of Amazon.in or Flipkart, a small panel shows the price over the last 90 days as a chart.
The panel says whether today's price is lower, the same or higher than the 90-day average.
The user can set a price alert for the product and get a browser notification when it drops below it.
The extension asks only for access to the two shopping sites and storage.
There is a privacy policy that says what is collected and sent.
There is a Chrome Web Store listing: description, screenshots and the permission reasons.

charter.statement: A REST API that lets clinics in Hyderabad manage patient appointments, used by their website and a mobile app.
charter.audience: Developers of the clinics' website and app; clinic administrators.
standards: Patient data is encrypted in transit and at rest.
Responses under 300 ms for 95% of requests at 50 requests per second.
rules: Follows India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act for patient data.
Every change to an appointment is logged with who made it.
done_when: There are endpoints to create, read, update and cancel appointments, documented in an OpenAPI file.
Clinics, doctors and their weekly schedules can be managed through the API.
Double booking of a doctor's slot is refused with a clear error.
Every request needs an API key or a signed-in user, and each role sees only what it is allowed to.
An audit log records every change with time, user and old and new values.
There is a deployment guide and a load test result showing the response-time standard is met.

charter.statement: A dashboard where a Jaipur handicrafts exporter uploads their monthly sales spreadsheet and sees sales by product, country and month.
charter.audience: The exporter's owner and 2 managers, not data experts.
standards: Every chart says what it shows in one line.
Numbers in rupees with Indian digit grouping.
rules: The data stays on the user's device.
No chart without its data table available.
done_when: The user uploads a CSV or Excel file with columns date, product, country, quantity and amount, and wrong columns get a clear message.
It shows total sales, orders and average order value for the chosen period.
It shows sales by month as a line chart and by country and by product as bar charts.
The user can filter by date range, country and product, and every chart updates.
It lists the top 10 products and the products whose sales fell most against the previous period.
The user can download any chart's data as CSV.

charter.statement: An online store for a Kolkata saree weaver that sells handwoven sarees across India with UPI and card payments.
charter.audience: Shoppers across India buying sarees online; the weaver's family who run the business.
standards: Product photos and descriptions state fabric, weave, length and care.
Prices in rupees including GST.
rules: Follows the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules: seller details, return policy and grievance officer shown.
Only claims of handloom that the weaver can prove are used.
done_when: Shoppers can browse sarees by fabric, colour and price, and see each saree's photos, details and price.
Shoppers can add sarees to a cart and pay by UPI or card through a licensed gateway.
Shoppers get an order confirmation with the order number by email or SMS.
The owners can add products, mark sarees as sold out and see new orders.
Shipping charges and delivery times by region are shown before payment.
The site shows the seller's details, the return and refund policy and the grievance officer.

charter.statement: A brand identity for a new specialty tea company in Darjeeling selling directly to young urban buyers online.
charter.audience: The founders and the designers and agencies they will brief; buyers aged 22 to 35 in Indian cities.
standards: The name is checked for existing trademarks in India in the tea class.
Colours pass WCAG AA contrast for text.
rules: No use of the protected 'Darjeeling' logo without permission.
No claims about health benefits.
done_when: It offers 5 name options with the reasoning, and recommends one after a trademark search note for each.
It states the brand's positioning, personality in 3 words and tone of voice with do and don't examples.
It describes a logo concept in words and the rules for using it.
It sets a colour palette with hex values and a type pairing with where each is used.
It gives a tagline and three sample messages: a product label, an Instagram post and a website hero line.
Everything is in one brand guide document.

charter.statement: A 30-day Instagram and LinkedIn content calendar for a Pune-based accounting firm that wants enquiries from small business owners.
charter.audience: Small business owners in Pune; the firm's 2 partners who will post the content.
standards: Every post has a goal: reach, trust or enquiry.
Tax facts are for the current financial year and marked to be checked by the partners.
rules: No promises of tax savings for a specific person.
Follows ICAI rules on advertising by chartered accountants.
done_when: The calendar has a post for every day for Instagram and 3 a week for LinkedIn, with date, format and goal.
Each post has its caption, hashtags and a description of the image or video.
At least 8 posts answer common tax questions of small businesses.
Each week has one post with a clear call to enquire and how to contact the firm.
Every post is marked as allowed under ICAI advertising rules, with a note where it is close to the line.
It says which numbers to track each week and what result counts as working.

charter.statement: A spreadsheet financial model for opening a second branch of a cafe in Mysuru, to decide if it pays back within 2 years.
charter.audience: The cafe owner and their bank's loan officer.
standards: Inputs, calculations and outputs are on separate sheets.
Every input has a note on where it came from.
rules: Loan interest and GST are calculated, not typed in.
No hidden rows or hard-coded numbers in formulas.
done_when: The inputs sheet has setup cost, rent, staff, average bill, footfall per day, food cost percentage and loan terms.
It calculates monthly revenue, costs, EMI and profit for 36 months.
It shows the payback month and whether it is within 24 months.
It has three scenarios (low, expected, high footfall) the user can switch between.
It has a sensitivity table of payback month against footfall and average bill.
A one-page summary sheet states the result in plain words for the loan officer.

charter.statement: An automation that takes every new enquiry from a coaching institute's website form, adds it to a Google Sheet, sends the student a WhatsApp welcome message and reminds a counsellor to call within 24 hours.
charter.audience: The institute's 3 counsellors and its owner.
standards: No enquiry is lost: every run is logged.
Messages follow WhatsApp Business messaging rules.
rules: Students who opt out get no more messages.
Student phone numbers are not shared outside the institute.
done_when: Each new form entry is added to the sheet within 5 minutes with name, phone, course and time.
The student gets a WhatsApp welcome message from an approved template.
A counsellor is assigned in turn and gets a reminder; if not marked called within 24 hours, the owner is told.
A student who replies STOP is marked opted out and gets no more messages.
Every run is logged with success or the error, and failures are retried once.
There is a one-page guide for the owner on how it works and how to switch it off.

charter.statement: An employee handbook and standard operating procedures for a 40-person software services company in Kochi.
charter.audience: Current and new employees; the HR manager and founders.
standards: Plain language, with a summary at the top of each policy.
Each policy names its owner and review date.
rules: Follows Indian labour law that applies in Kerala, including the POSH Act.
No policy contradicts another.
done_when: It covers working hours, leave, holidays, remote work, expenses, code of conduct and IT security.
It has a POSH policy with the Internal Committee and how to raise a complaint.
It has step-by-step SOPs for onboarding, offboarding and raising an expense claim.
Each policy says which law or rule it follows, where one applies.
There is an acknowledgement form employees sign.
A list of open questions for the founders marks anything the handbook had to assume.

charter.statement: A 24-page illustrated children's ebook in English about a girl in Kerala who learns to swim, for ages 4 to 7.
charter.audience: Children aged 4 to 7 and the parents who read with them.
standards: Sentences a 6-year-old can follow, at most 2 per page.
Shows water safety correctly.
rules: No frightening scenes.
Illustration briefs avoid stereotypes.
done_when: The story has a clear beginning, problem and happy ending across 24 pages.
Each page has its text and a brief for the illustrator.
The swimming and safety details are correct, with an adult present in every water scene.
There is a title, a cover brief and a back-cover blurb.
There are 3 questions for parents to ask after reading.
The words used are checked against a list suitable for ages 4 to 7.
